content: Agronomy is a specialized branch of agricultural science that focuses on the study of crops and the soils in which they grow. Agronomists are dedicated to developing advanced methods to optimize soil usage and enhance the production of food and fiber crops. Their work involves conducting research in various areas, including crop rotation, irrigation and drainage systems, plant breeding techniques, soil classification, soil fertility management, weed control strategies, and other related fields. Agronomy is defined as the science of utilizing plants, animals, and soils to produce food, fuel, feed, fiber, and other essential resources. Agriculture, on the other hand, is the science, art, and practice of farming. It encompasses the cultivation of soil for growing crops and the rearing of animals to produce food, wool, and other agricultural products. In the context of soil, it is estimated that 80 to 99% of microorganisms present in soil remain unidentified. At the Arlington Agricultural Research Station, the soil is classified as Plano silt-loam, containing 4% organic matter and extending to a depth of 25 meters. Soil cores with a diameter of 5 cm were collected from the top 10 cm of a clover-grass pasture. These soil samples were immediately placed on dry ice, homogenized, and stored at -70°C before undergoing DNA extraction. Soil analysis was performed by the Soil Testing Laboratory at the University of Wisconsin—Madison, following the methodology described by Schulte et al. The soil was found to contain 0.3% total nitrogen, 400 ppm of potassium (K+), and 98 ppm of phosphorus (P). The site is well-drained, with groundwater located more than 25 meters below the surface. Approximately two-thirds of the annual rainfall, which averages 79 cm, occurs between April and October. The site experiences an average of 165 frost-free days per year.
